transcript.text: fridge part freezin stuff, lettuce + yoghurts frozen solid at the back. hotpoint ff. any ideas pls

Yes — the usual causes are a fridge setting that is too cold, food pressed against the cold rear wall/air outlet, or less commonly a temperature-control fault. 1. Check the temperature setting. Aim for about 3–5°C in the fridge, with the control around its middle setting rather than maximum cold. Also check that any Super Cool/Fast Freeze function is not on. If it was set very cold, turn it down and allow 24 hours with the door kept shut; that points to a settings issue. 2. Move food away from the back wall and any vents by a few centimetres. Items against the rear can freeze even if the overall fridge temperature is normal. Lettuce is especially vulnerable. 3. If you have a fridge thermometer, put it on the middle shelf, not against the back. Below about 1–2°C suggests the fridge is genuinely over-cooling rather than just creating a cold patch. If it is on a normal setting, nothing is touching the back, and food continues to freeze after a day or two, the more likely fault is the thermostat/temperature sensor or an air flap letting too much freezer air into the fridge. That is usually an engineer repair rather than a setting adjustment.
dial was on max, kids prob moved it. fridge is rammed after big shop and stuff is pushed against the back vents. will turn dial to middle and clear them

That is very likely the cause rather than a failed part: maximum cold plus food pressed against the back vents can easily freeze items solid in that area. Set the dial around the middle, leave a small gap around the rear vents/back wall, and avoid packing the fridge so tightly that air cannot circulate. Give it 24–48 hours with the door kept shut as much as practical; a big fresh shop also makes it work harder while it cools everything down. If food no longer freezes, it was a settings/loading issue. If it still freezes at the back with the dial in the middle and space around the vents, the next likely causes are the temperature control/sensor or an air flap letting in too much freezer air, and that would need an engineer to diagnose.
ok did that. 2 days on its better but one yoghurt still froze right at the very back. is that normal?

One yoghurt freezing right at the very back can still be normal, especially so soon after the dial was on maximum and the fridge was heavily loaded. The fact it is otherwise better is reassuring. The rear wall/air outlet is usually the coldest spot, so keep dairy, salad and other easily frozen items on a middle or front shelf rather than at the back. The useful next check is the overall fridge temperature on the middle shelf, away from the rear wall. It should be about 3–5°C. If it is in that range and only items left at the back freeze, treat it as a local cold spot rather than a fault. If the middle shelf is around 1–2°C or below, or food away from the back starts freezing too, the likely cause becomes the temperature control/sensor or an air damper fault, and an engineer should diagnose it rather than changing parts blindly.

candidates: Temperature set too cold, or super-cool/fast-freeze left on (high)
Food touching the cold back wall or cold-air outlet (high)
Temperature sensor/thermostat or air-damper control fault (medium)
